messages:
marta: Heads up — staging AWQ canary for the new gpt-2-compat model is showing nondeterministic decode divergence after ~2k tokens when group_size=64 + act_quant=on. Paused the canary and rolled back. Logs show token mismatches across replicas.

ajay: ugh. can you paste the reproduce command and an example mismatch snippet?

marta: repro command (run on a single replica):

```
REPRO_CMD=\"./serve_model --model gpt2-compat-awq --quant awq --group_size 64 --act_quant true --seed 42 --batch_size 8 --max_tokens 3000\"
$REPRO_CMD
```

mismatch example: 
```
[2026-03-18T14:12:33Z] decode divergence at step=2156 expected=\"the\" got=\"their\" (replica A vs B)
```

ryan: interesting — i ran that exact cmd but with seed=42 and didn't hit it. try seed=7?

marta: tried seeds 7,13,42,100 across 5 runs each. summary: seeds [7,13,101] -> flip-rate 6–12% after 2k tokens; seeds [42,100] -> 0.5–1% flip-rate. so it's seed-sensitive, not purely per-request non-determinism.

sophia: could be activation-quant kernel rounding + accumulation order. act-quant is per-channel scale with nearest rounding at the moment, right?

ajay: yep per-channel, rounding=nearest. also check group ordering — our AWQ dynamic grouping can change internal accumulation order, which affects fp->int conversions. small nondet can amplify in long sequences.

marta: pasted the actq config we used: 
```
act_q_config={
  \"per_channel\": true,
  \"rounding\": \"nearest\",
  \"zero_point\": 0
}
```

ajay: quick mitigations to keep canary up: set act_quant=false OR increase group_size to 128 to reduce boundary effects, AND force deterministic kernels: `export REDWOOD_DETERMINISTIC=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`. but that will push latency up.

ryan: also try disabling prefix cache for repro — prefix cache changes ordering of kv reads occasionally which can expose nondet.

sophia: good call. add `--prefix_cache=false` to the repro runs.

marta: plan: i'll run a small grid tonight: group_size in [32,64,128], actq on/off, seeds [7,42,101], prefix_cache on/off. measure token flip-rate, p50/p99 latency, and throughput. will post CSV.

ajay: also add an experiment toggling `actq_rounding` between nearest and stochastic (if available) to see sensitivity.

ci-bot: Canary rollback executed for deployment gpt2-compat-awq (canary id c-20260318-17).

deploy-bot: Rollback complete — traffic shifted back to stable.

marta: thanks. scheduling an infra profiler run to capture instruction-level diffs on the worst seeds and will open a tiny reproducer PR for eng-runtime to add deterministic quant kernels flag. @eng-runtime fyi.

ryan: if we confirm it's accumulation order, another mitigation is to use group-aware stable accumulation (accumulate in deterministic tile order) — may be a medium-term fix.

sophia: add note: for production rollouts, we should require flip-rate < 0.5% on the longest eval sequences (>=2k tokens) before canary.

marta: agreed. i'll post results in the morning and link the csv + repro artifacts. thanks all :thumbsup:
